description:
FILED s420 by the #410 measurement (the residue that task names as
"E5-adjacent naming work").

    { package ＦＯＯ; our $z = 5; sub bar { 1 } }
    print exists $ＦＯＯ::{bar} ? 1 : 0;     # perl: 1   PCL: 0
    my $g = delete $ＦＯＯ::{bar};            # perl: y   PCL: n

The statements LOWER correctly now (#410); the emission is
`(p-defpackage :ＦＯＯ)` and `(p-stash "ＦＯＯ")`, which look consistent.  They
are not, and the reason is the CL reader, measured s420:

  * SBCL NFKC-normalizes symbol names read from source, so the fullwidth Ｆ
    (U+FF26) in the DESIGNATOR becomes an ASCII F;
  * generated code loads under :invert, so the now-all-caps FOO reads as
    "foo".
  Result: (read-from-string ":ＦＯＯ") has symbol-name "foo" (char codes
  102 111 111), while the runtime string stays "ＦＯＯ" (65318 65327 65327).
  PIPE-QUOTING defeats both: ":|ＦＯＯ|" reads back as 65318 65327 (measured).

FIX SHAPE: pipe-quote a package designator that carries a non-ASCII character,
wherever one is emitted.  The rule today is `$pkg =~ /::/ ? "|$pkg|" : $pkg`
and there is more than one copy of it (grep first —
feedback_check_for_a_second_copy).  Scalars and subs in such a package already
work (`$ＦＯＯ::z`, `Ａ::f()`) because they go through qualified_var_to_cl,
which pipe-quotes; it is the bare single-segment designator that does not.

Acceptance: the uni/ stash rows of #410's probe file, plus an inverse guard
that an ASCII package name's emission is byte-identical.

s421 (Fable review) — SCOPE WIDENED: the same reader mechanism collides
VARIABLES, not only package designators, and it is a SILENT WRONG:

    use utf8; our %Ｘ=(a=>1); our %X=(a=>2); our $Ｘ=5; our $X=6;
    print $Ｘ{a}, $X{a}, $Ｘ, $X, "\n";     # perl 1256   PCL 2266

`%Ｘ` and `%X` are ONE CL symbol: the emission is the bare `%Ｘ`, SBCL's
reader NFKC-folds U+FF38 to `X`, and `:invert` then down-cases it (the
backtrace prints the symbol as |%x|).  So the fix rule is: ANY emitted
symbol whose name carries a non-ASCII character is pipe-quoted — package
designators, variables of every sigil, sub names (`sub Ｆ {}` beside
`sub F {}` — probe), and `p-stash`/stash keys stay the raw string.  Only
NFKC-compatibility characters fold (fullwidth forms, ligatures, superscripts;
the uni/ test files use fullwidth deliberately); ordinary non-ASCII letters
(é, ж, 日) survive NFKC and only meet `:invert`, which is consistent as long
as both definition and use go through the reader — which is exactly what
`p-stash "ＦＯＯ"` does NOT do.  Acceptance adds this probe; inverse guard:
ASCII emission byte-identical (tools/emission-ab.pl over the populations).


DONE s423 (Opus, 2026-08-22), branch worktree-agent-ac24c08623154686e â
`docs/opus5-review-requests-s423.md`.

THE RULE, in one place: Pl::CLForm::cl_sym / cl_pkg.  A perl NAME that becomes
a CL TOKEN is spelled there; a perl name that stays a STRING (p-stash key,
method name, hash key) is untouched.  cl_sym is the IDENTITY on ASCII â that
is the correctness condition, not a convenience: under :invert a bare `$x`
reads as `$X` while `|$x|` reads as `$x`, so quoting an ASCII name would
RENAME it.  The four `$pkg =~ /::/ ? "|$pkg|" : $pkg` copies were folded into
the helper; a fifth lived OUTSIDE Pl/, in pl2cl's build_eval_preamble.
Runtime half: %pcl-invert-case is the identity on a name carrying a non-ASCII
character, which makes "pipe-quoted" mean "verbatim" on both sides of the
seam and fixes every intern site at once.

MEASURED.  New instrument = "a non-ASCII character in a BARE token in the
emitted CL" (not inside |â¦|, a string, a ;-comment or #\c): 1962 occurrences
across 49 files at a2ac578, ZERO across 404 emitted files (uni/ mro/ op/ re/)
after.  emission-ab over perl-tests/*.t + perl's own t/ + lib/**/*.pm = 738
files, 686 SAME, RCDIFF 0, and the 52 DIFF files are EXACTLY the 52 whose base
emission carried such a token (52 of 52).  corpus-diff identical, drops 7
unchanged.  Gate 156/5655 cold, failures exactly the 13 pclxs xs rows.  Sweep GATE clean,
TOTAL 18365 (+0), drops 7 = census.  Companion uni/+mro/: 16 movers, 15 gains
(three mro utf8 files FULLY PASSING and de-registered; 18 expected-rows
narrowed away); the ONE loss is uni/gv.t 53/28 -> 50/31 = three ACCIDENTAL
passes on `local *NAME` (#433, ASCII-identical).  Rebased onto 04ebd7b;
generation v2-171 (main had moved to v2-170, so the brief's v2-165 would have
been LOWER than main's).
28 probes vs perl 5.40.3.

THREE SEAMS the first pass missed, each found by probing, not by reading:
 (a) pl2cl's build_eval_preamble â its own designator copy, so a string eval
     inside `package ï¼¦ï¼¯ï¼¯` resolved globals in a DIFFERENT package;
 (b) `open ï¼¦ï¼¨`/`close ï¼¦ï¼¨` emitted bare while `print ï¼¦ï¼¨`/`<ï¼¦ï¼¨>` quoted â
     the program wrote to one handle and read from another, printing NOTHING.
     Fixed at the leaf, keyed on the `is_filehandle` registry;
 (c) _swap_elem_sigil knew `Foo::$x` and `|$ï¼¸|` but not `Foo::|$ï¼¸|`, so
     `"$main::ï¼¬[0]"` handed p-aref the SCALAR and died in gethash.

WHAT NOT TO RETRY: a blanket cl_sym on every PPI::Token::Word in gen_leaf.
That leaf is a MIXED site â it also carries text already rewritten to a
qualified CL symbol and fed BACK to cl_name as a perl name, where
`|ï¼¦ï¼¯ï¼¯::f|` splits on `::` into the package `|ï¼¦ï¼¯ï¼¯` and the whole file
fails to READ.  cl_sym/cl_pkg now treat any `|` in the input as "already a CL
spelling", so a double pass is a no-op rather than a corruption.

RESIDUE, all PRE-EXISTING and identical for ASCII names (which is the evidence
#418 is closed rather than narrowed): #430 (keys %Pkg:: lists only subs),
#431 (AUTOLOAD not consulted for a qualified sub call), #432 (runpcl's
spurious blank line falsifies a byte-compare).

Guard: Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t, 21 rows, incl. two ASCII inverse rows.
title: A non-ASCII PACKAGE name: the CL designator is NFKC-normalized and inverted, the runtime string is not
